{
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "EPA-approved test procedures (methods) for the analysis and quantification of pollutants or pollutant parameters, including for the purposes of compliance monitoring/DMR reporting, permit renewal applications, or any other reporting that may be required as a condition of this permit, shall be sufficiently sensitive.",
      "affected_purpose": "B",
      "computation_change_reason": "Whether a reporting activity counts as required compliance monitoring/DMR reporting under this clause affects which monitoring obligations are in scope for FY2025 and whether method-sensitivity requirements attach to a given requirement."
    },
    {
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "A method is \"sufficiently sensitive\" when (1) the method minimum level (ML) of quantification is at or below the level of the applicable effluent limit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter;",
      "affected_purpose": "A,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Interpretation of which effluent limit is 'applicable' and whether the method ML is at or below that limit determines whether a reported value is treated as a valid numeric compliance comparison (Purpose A) versus a non-comparable or missing-evidence case such as below-quantification reporting (Purpose C)."
    },
    {
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "or (2) if there is no EPA-approved analytical method with a published ML at or below the effluent limit (see table below), then the method has the lowest published ML (is the most sensitive) of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR Part 136 or required under 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapters N or O, for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter;",
      "affected_purpose": "A,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Whether the no-method-at-limit condition is met and which method qualifies as the lowest published ML changes the effective quantification threshold used for limit exceedance analysis (Purpose A) and how sub-ML or non-detect results are classified when ordinary numeric comparison is not possible (Purpose C)."
    },
    {
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "or (3) the method is specified in this permit or has been otherwise approved in writing by the permitting authority (EPA Region 6) for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter.",
      "affected_purpose": "A,B",
      "computation_change_reason": "A different reading of whether a method is permit-specified or has written EPA Region 6 approval changes which analytical method is required for monitoring (Purpose B) and therefore which sensitivity standard governs numeric compliance evaluation (Purpose A)."
    },
    {
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "The Permittee has the option of developing and submitting a report to justify the use of matrix or sample-specific MLs rather than the published levels. Upon written approval by EPA Region 6 the matrix or sample-specific MLs may be utilized by the Permittee for all future Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting requirements.",
      "affected_purpose": "A,B,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Whether matrix or sample-specific MLs were approved in writing changes the quantification level applied to DMR data, which alters monitoring-method obligations (Purpose B), whether reported values can be compared to effluent limits (Purpose A), and how missing or below-ML results are characterized (Purpose C)."
    },
    {
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "Current EPA Region 6 minimum quantification levels (MQLs) for reporting and compliance are provided in Appendix A of Part II of this permit.",
      "affected_purpose": "A,B",
      "computation_change_reason": "Treating Appendix A MQLs as binding for 'compliance' versus reporting-only changes which numeric threshold is used to evaluate measurements against limits (Purpose A) and which quantification standards apply to required monitoring (Purpose B)."
    },
    {
      "source": "farmington/final_permit.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 10, Section part_i",
      "exact_span": "The following pollutants may not have EPA-approved methods with a published ML at or below the effluent limit, if specified:",
      "affected_purpose": "A,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Interpretation of which pollutants are 'specified' in the referenced table and whether the no-method-at-limit pathway applies changes whether standard effluent-limit comparison rules or the alternate lowest-ML rule governs, affecting exceedance determinations (Purpose A) and classification of non-quantifiable results (Purpose C)."
    }
  ]
}
